best_for: Deezer subscribers on Windows or Mac who want their music in a desktop window with keyboard shortcuts and offline downloads, rather than a browser tab.
description:
Deezer is a music and podcast streaming service, and this is its desktop app. Deezer labels tracks that its system detects were made with AI, so you can tell at a glance, and it pays artists through what it calls an Artist-Centric Payment System.

Start Flow and it plays an endless mix of your favorites and new finds, set to a mood or style. Bring your playlists and favorites over from another streaming service, sing along with lyrics and translate them, or use Shaker to pull a group of friends' music into one playlist. My Deezer Month and My Deezer Year recap what you played. The desktop app also has hours of video, from live sessions to interviews.

points.title: The app is free, the music mostly isn't
points.text: The Free plan plays with ads, does not let you pick any track you like, and has no offline listening or high-fidelity sound. Those come with a paid plan, and every paid plan starts with a one-month free trial.

points.title: US plan prices
points.text: Premium is USD 11.99 a month or USD 107.99 a year, Student USD 5.99 a month, Duo USD 15.99 a month for two accounts, and Family USD 19.99 a month for six. Prices are from the US page and were read on the date below.

points.title: Offline needs a subscription
points.text: Downloading tracks for offline listening in the desktop app works on Premium, Family, Student and HiFi plans only.

points.title: No Linux app
points.text: Deezer makes the desktop app for Windows and macOS only; its download page lists no Linux build.

points.title: Installs per user
points.text: The Windows installer is 32-bit and installs for the current user, so no administrator rights are needed. The Mac build is universal and needs macOS 12 or later.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 66 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
